messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — severity P1. Tenant= NEXAHEALTH (dedicated pool: vpc-us-e-2). Elevated tail latency and ~12% 5xx rate for text-generation endpoints. Detected at 2026-03-15T02:57Z. Paging Jamie (primary) and Maria (backup).
jamie: I'm on it. seeing a spike in queue_len for nxh-tenant-001: queue depth jumped from 10 -> 120 in last 3m, p95 latency ~6.2s. Confirming customer is on a dedicated pool with autoscale disabled.
ryan: Is this traffic pattern expected? Any scheduled jobs from NexaHealth? @nora from CS?
nora: Not that I know of. They did a model change last week but nothing scheduled. I'll open a ticket and ping their infra contact.
elaine: Dumping recent scheduler metrics from the host; looks like batching size is hitting max_batch_tokens=512 for many requests, which causes long batching windows. p99 queue wait ~4.5s.
jamie: Good catch. Looks like their load pattern is many small requests but some long-context requests which allow huge batches to form. Need tenant-specific tuning: reduce max_batch_tokens and cap batch sizes.
maria: Recommend immediate mitigations: 1) set tenant scheduler_mode=latency-first, 2) max_batch_tokens=64, 3) max_batch_size=8, 4) enable tenant queue_throttle at 350 qps. We can roll back after verification.
jamie: I'll apply changes via admin API. Applying one change at a time to observe impact. First step: switch scheduler_mode.
jamie: ```
# switching scheduler to latency-first for tenant
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/v1/tenants/nxh-001/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scheduler_mode":"latency-first"}'
```
ops-bot: Command accepted. Config update queued and will be applied cluster-wide. Change id: cfg-98312.
ops-bot: Applying change now to vpc-us-e-2. Rolling update across nodes (max 2 nodes concurrently).
jamie: Change applied to 3/3 nodes in the pool. Observed immediate ~20% improvement in p95 but still elevated p99 due to lingering large batches.
ryan: Proceed with batch token and batch size limits.
jamie: Applying: ```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/v1/tenants/nxh-001/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"max_batch_tokens":64, "max_batch_size":8}'
```
ops-bot: Config change cfg-98313 accepted. Propagating to pool.
ops-bot: cfg-98313 applied to nodes 1/3.
jamie: cfg-98313 applied to all nodes. Early metrics: p95 latency down from 6.2s -> 1.3s, p99 from 8.9s -> 2.6s. Error rate dropping: 5xx from 12% -> 1.8% in last 60s.
maria: Nice. Can we also enable temporary fallbacks for long-context requests to a lower-latency model variant? That will stop a few heavy requests from waiting.
jamie: Routing small fraction (10%) of requests with context_len > 2048 to gptq-3b-lowlat using routing policy.
jamie: ```
redwoodctl routing update --tenant nxh-001 --rule 'if context_len>2048 then route model=gptq-3b-lowlat weight=10%'
```
ops-bot: Routing rule updated. Rule id: route-4421.
elaine: Metrics after 3m: aggregate throughput stable, p95 holds ~1.2s, p99 ~2.4s. Queue depth back to baseline ~9-15. Customer error budget appears intact now.
nora: Notifying NexaHealth support contact per runbook. Ticket created: NXH-7831. CC: infra@NexaHealth.
nora: Suggested customer-facing note: 'We observed transient queuing on your dedicated pool causing elevated latency. We applied tenant-specific scheduling and batch caps which reduced tail latency and error rate. Monitoring continues.'
jamie: Sent comms to customer. They acknowledged and asked if this will recur when traffic spikes. I'll propose an ops play: enable autoscale for dedicated pool or increase reserved capacity during peak windows.
maria: For immediate safety, I'll enable tenant-level queue_throttle to limit incoming QPS to 350 to avoid re-queueing surge traffic.
jamie: Enabling queue_throttle now.
jamie: ```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/v1/tenants/nxh-001/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"queue_throttle_qps":350}'
```
ops-bot: queue_throttle applied. Throttle active on vpc-us-e-2.
jamie: After throttle: ingress QPS smoothed, no further 5xx spikes. Customer requests not dropped (requests queued/timed in gracefully). We'll keep throttle for 2 hours and plan follow-up.
ryan: Action items before handoff: - Create alert that fires on sustained queue depth > 50 for tenant nxh-001 - Propose autoscale for vpc-us-e-2 or reserve + burst capacity - Add regression test to evals for mixed small+long-context workload
jamie: I'll add the first alert and a Runbook note explaining the knob sequence we used (scheduler_mode -> max_batch_tokens -> max_batch_size -> routing fallback -> queue_throttle). Tagging doc: runbooks/tenant-batch-mitigation.
maria: Handing off to Night oncall @maria (04:00-12:00 UTC). Current state: stable, p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~2.5s, 5xx ~1.6%. Monitor for 45m then consider removing queue_throttle if stable.
maria: Key things for next oncall: keep an eye on queue depth and model routing ratio, don't revert max_batch_tokens until stable for 24h. If errors return, escalate to infra and consider temporary pool scale-up.
jamie: Notes for postmortem: timeline, metrics, customer impact (~12% requests saw errors for ~7m), root cause: mixed request-size pattern + large max_batch_tokens allowed long batching windows, mitigations applied. Assign owners: postmortem writeup -> Jamie, autoscale proposal -> Ryan, customer follow-up -> Nora.
nora: I'll prepare customer follow-up email and offer to schedule a short sync on autoscaling options.
elaine: Adding a suggested improvement to scheduler: make default tenant max_batch_tokens adaptive by observing token-length distribution for past 30m. Will file a design ticket.
jamie: Closing the paging for now. If anyone sees new 5xx or queue depth >50 ping here and page P1. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident resolved (P1 -> mitigated). Alert will remain in-monitoring for 1h."
